attrs.label: What holds WordPress sites back
attrs.html:
What holds WordPress sites back

WordPress is good for SEO out of the box. Years of plugins, themes and quick fixes are what slow it down. This is the Plugins screen of a typical site we’re asked to look at.

  1. 1

    Too many plugins

    Every plugin adds code. Most sites we audit run 25 to 40, and a third are doing nothing at all.

  2. 2

    Page builders

    Elementor, WPBakery and Divi load heavy CSS and JavaScript on every page, even where it isn’t used.

  3. 3

    Duplicate archives

    Tag, category, author, date and attachment pages create hundreds of thin URLs that compete with your real pages.

  4. 4

    Slow hosting and old PHP

    Cheap shared hosting and PHP 7 can double the time before the page even starts to load.

  5. 5

    SEO plugins fighting

    Two SEO plugins print two titles, two canonicals and two sitemaps. Google picks one, often the wrong one.

  6. 6

    Out-of-date and hacked

    An outdated plugin is the most common way in for spam pages, hidden links and redirects.

attrs.label: What our WordPress SEO services include
attrs.html:
What our WordPress SEO services include

WordPress SEO optimisation from people who work inside WordPress every day. Each fix is made where it belongs: in the theme, the settings or the server, not with another plugin.

Technical WordPress SEO

WordPress creates far more URLs than most owners realise: tag, category, author, date and attachment archives, paginated lists, feeds and search pages. Left alone, Google spends its time on these instead of your services and products. We set up a clean structure where every important page has one URL, one canonical and a clear place in the site.

What we do

  • Permalinks set to clean, readable URLs, with 301 redirects from the old ones
  • Thin archives (tags, authors, dates, attachments) noindexed or turned into useful pages
  • One canonical version of the site: https, with or without www
  • XML sitemaps that list only the pages you want in Google
  • robots.txt and Search Console set up, errors fixed
  • Broken links and redirect chains cleaned up

Where we work in WordPressSettings → Permalinks · Yoast or Rank Math → Search appearance · .htaccess

What you getFewer junk URLs in Google, and your key pages crawled and indexed faster.

Speed and Core Web Vitals

Most slow WordPress sites aren’t slow because of WordPress. They’re slow because of a heavy theme, a page builder loading everything everywhere, 30 plugins and cheap hosting. Our developers find what’s actually costing time on each template and fix it at the source, rather than stacking another speed plugin on top.

What we do

  • Plugin audit: keep, replace or remove each one
  • Page caching, object caching and a CDN set up correctly
  • Images converted to WebP or AVIF and served at the right size
  • Critical CSS inlined, unused CSS and JavaScript removed or delayed
  • Third-party scripts (chat, tracking, fonts) loaded only when needed
  • PHP upgraded and hosting reviewed, with a move if it’s needed

Where we work in WordPressfunctions.php · WP Rocket or LiteSpeed Cache · Cloudflare · hosting panel

What you getPages that pass Core Web Vitals on mobile, and visitors who stay.

On-page SEO

Every page that matters gets a clear target search, a title and description people want to click, a sensible heading structure and links from related pages. We work in your editor, whether that’s the block editor, Elementor or another builder, so your team can keep it up afterwards.

What we do

  • Keyword targeting for each service, product and category page
  • Titles and meta descriptions rewritten for clicks, not just keywords
  • One H1 per page and a heading structure that makes sense
  • Internal links from blog posts to the pages that make money
  • Image alt text and file names that describe the image
  • Pages competing for the same search merged or refocused

Where we work in WordPressPage editor · Yoast or Rank Math box · Media library

What you getMore of your pages on page one, and more clicks from the same rankings.

Schema markup

Structured data tells Google and AI search tools what your pages are about: your business, your services, your products and your articles. Many WordPress sites have none, or have three overlapping versions from the theme, the SEO plugin and a review plugin. We set up one clean, valid set.

What we do

  • Organization or LocalBusiness with your logo, address and profiles
  • BreadcrumbList on every page
  • Article and author markup on blog posts
  • Product, Offer and Review on WooCommerce products
  • FAQPage only where the questions are visible on the page
  • Duplicate and broken schema from themes and plugins removed

Where we work in WordPressJSON-LD in the theme · SEO plugin schema settings

What you getPages eligible for rich results, and a site AI answers can understand.

Content and site structure

Rankings come from having the right pages, not just tidy ones. We map the searches your customers make to pages on your site, find the gaps, and plan new service pages, category pages and articles, with a structure that shows Google how they fit together.

What we do

  • Keyword research and a page-by-page plan
  • New service, location and category pages where there are gaps
  • Blog articles that answer questions and link to your services
  • Categories and menus organised around how people search
  • Old, thin posts updated, merged or removed
  • A content calendar your team or ours can follow

Where we work in WordPressPages · Posts · Categories · Menus

What you getTraffic from searches you weren’t showing up for.

Security and site health

Outdated plugins are the most common way into a WordPress site, and hacked sites get spam pages, hidden links and warnings in Google. Keeping the site healthy protects your rankings as much as your data.

What we do

  • WordPress, theme and plugins updated safely, with backups
  • Unused themes and plugins deleted
  • Spam users, comments and injected pages cleaned up
  • SSL, security headers and login protection checked
  • Site Health brought to “Good”
  • Uptime monitoring and alerts

Where we work in WordPressTools → Site Health · Plugins · Users

What you getFewer risks, and no surprises in Search Console.

Local SEO for WordPress

For businesses that serve an area, the website and the Google Business Profile have to tell the same story. We build location pages that rank, keep your name, address and phone number consistent everywhere, and connect the site to your profile so both get stronger.

What we do

  • Location and service-area pages with real local content
  • LocalBusiness schema with address, hours and service areas
  • Name, address and phone number consistent across the site
  • Google Business Profile linked, with the right landing page
  • Embedded maps and directions that don’t slow the page
  • Reviews shown on the site, with valid markup

Where we work in WordPressPages · Yoast Local SEO or Rank Math Local · theme footer

What you getMore calls and visits from people searching nearby.

WooCommerce SEO

WooCommerce turns every product variation, filter and sort order into a new URL. We decide which pages deserve to rank (usually categories and main products), keep the rest out of the index, and give products the schema Google needs to show price, stock and reviews.

What we do

  • Category pages with useful copy, not just a product grid
  • One canonical URL per product, whatever category it sits in
  • Variation and filter URLs kept out of the index
  • Product, Offer and Review schema with price and stock
  • Out-of-stock and discontinued products handled without losing rankings
  • Product images named, compressed and described

Where we work in WordPressWooCommerce → Settings → Products · product templates · SEO plugin

What you getProducts and categories that show price, stock and stars in Google.

Redesigns and migrations

A new theme, a new domain or a move to WordPress from another platform is when most sites lose traffic. We plan the move with your developers: every old URL mapped to its new home, content and metadata carried over, and the launch checked the same day.

What we do

  • Crawl and benchmark of the old site before anything changes
  • A redirect map for every URL that has traffic or links
  • Titles, meta, headings and schema carried over to new templates
  • Staging site checked and kept out of Google
  • Launch-day checks: redirects, robots.txt, sitemaps, analytics
  • Rankings and traffic watched for 8 weeks after launch

Where we work in WordPressRedirection plugin or server rules · staging · Search Console

What you getA new site that keeps the traffic the old one earned.

Multilingual SEO

WPML, Polylang and TranslatePress all make translating easy, and all make it easy to get hreflang, URLs and sitemaps wrong. We set up each language so Google shows the right version to the right people, with translated URLs and metadata, not just translated text.

What we do

  • Language folders or domains chosen for your markets
  • hreflang tags that link every version both ways
  • Translated slugs, titles and meta descriptions
  • Sitemaps per language submitted to Search Console
  • No automatic redirects that block Googlebot
  • Keyword research per language, not word-for-word translation

Where we work in WordPressWPML, Polylang or TranslatePress settings · SEO plugin per language

What you getVisitors in each country land on their own language and prices.

Tracking and reporting

SEO is only worth what it brings in. We make sure every enquiry, call and sale from organic search is tracked correctly, then report on it every month in plain words: what changed, what it did and what we’re doing next.

What we do

  • Google Analytics 4 and Search Console connected and checked
  • Form submissions, calls and WooCommerce sales tracked as conversions
  • Tag Manager set up without slowing the site
  • A monthly dashboard of rankings, traffic and leads
  • A short written summary with next steps
  • Quarterly reviews of what’s working and what to change

Where we work in WordPressSite Kit by Google · Google Tag Manager · Looker Studio

What you getClear numbers on the leads and sales SEO brings in.

attrs.label: SEO for WooCommerce stores
attrs.html:
SEO for WooCommerce stores

Running a shop on WordPress? WooCommerce adds its own problems: variations, filters and product schema. These are the five we fix most often.

  1. 1

    Breadcrumbs and category paths

    The same product reached through several categories creates duplicate URLs. We set one primary category and canonical.

  2. 2

    Review stars in search

    Reviews need valid Review and AggregateRating schema, or the stars never show in Google.

  3. 3

    Prices and sale prices

    Product and Offer schema must carry the price, currency and stock, or the product isn’t eligible for rich results.

  4. 4

    Colour and size variations

    Variation URLs with ?attribute_pa_ parameters get crawled as separate pages. We point them to the main product.

  5. 5

    Out-of-stock products

    Deleting them loses their rankings. We keep the page, show alternatives and mark availability correctly.

Larger store, or not on WordPress? See our eCommerce SEO services.

attrs.label: WordPress SEO for AI search
attrs.html:
WordPress SEO for AI search

More of your customers now get answers from Google’s AI Overviews and ChatGPT before they click anything. These tools cite websites they can read, understand and trust. A well-built WordPress site can be one of them.

  • Schema that describes you

    AI answers lean on structured facts. We give every key page clean JSON-LD: who you are, what you offer, where, at what price, with which reviews.

    • Organization, LocalBusiness and Service schema
    • Product, Offer and Review on WooCommerce
    • Author and Article markup for expertise

  • Content AI can quote

    AI tools pick passages that answer a question directly. We structure pages so the answer is easy to find and lift.

    • A clear answer in the first two sentences
    • Question headings with short, direct answers
    • Tables, lists and facts, not just paragraphs

  • Crawl access for AI

    If AI crawlers can’t read your pages, you can’t be cited. Many WordPress security and caching set-ups block them by accident.

    • robots.txt rules for Googlebot, GPTBot and others
    • Firewall and bot settings that don’t block AI crawlers
    • Fast, server-rendered HTML, not content hidden in scripts

Want to go further? See our generative engine optimisation (GEO) services.

attrs.label: Your SEO plugin says green. Your rankings disagree.
attrs.html:
Your SEO plugin says green. Your rankings disagree.

Yoast, Rank Math and free SEO checkers are useful, and we use them too. But a plugin scores a page against a checklist. It can’t tell you why you’re not ranking, what your competitors do better, or what to fix first on your site. That takes a tailored WordPress SEO audit and someone who has seen hundreds of WordPress sites.

What the plugin sees

SEO analysis Good

/services/interior-design/ · focus keyphrase “bespoke interiors studio”

Good results (6)

  • Focus keyphrase in the SEO title
  • Meta description length
  • Keyphrase in the introduction
  • Images have alt attributes
  • Outbound and internal links
  • Text length: 820 words

What a tailored audit finds on the same page

  1. The page is slow

    LCP is 5.8 s on mobile because the page builder loads 1.4 MB of scripts. The plugin never measures speed.

  2. It targets the wrong search

    “bespoke interiors studio” gets 10 searches a month. “interior designer london” gets 2,400, and you rank on page 3.

  3. Google is choosing other pages

    860 tag, author and attachment pages are indexed and compete with this one.

  4. Competitors have what you don’t

    The top 3 results all show projects, prices and reviews. This page has none of them.

Free plugins and tools

  • Checks one page at a time, against a fixed list
  • A green light for keywords nobody searches
  • Can’t see speed, hosting, plugins or server settings
  • Doesn’t know your competitors or your market
  • Hundreds of warnings, no order of priority
  • No one to ask what to do next

A tailored WordPress SEO audit

  • Looks at the whole site: templates, plugins, hosting and code
  • Starts from the searches your customers actually make
  • Compares you with the sites that outrank you
  • Ranks every fix by impact on leads and sales
  • Recommendations written for your theme and builder
  • A walkthrough call with the consultant who did it

Every WordPress site is different. Your theme, builder, plugins, hosting and market decide what matters. A tailored audit gives you recommendations for your site, in the order that brings results fastest.

attrs.label: WordPress SEO myths, busted
attrs.html:
WordPress SEO myths, busted

Things we hear on almost every first call, and what’s actually true.

MythFactDetails
MythA green Yoast score means the page will rank. FactIt only means the page passed a checklist. DetailsThe score checks one page against fixed rules. Rankings depend on search demand, competitors, links, speed and whether the page answers the search.
MythMore plugins mean more features. FactMore plugins usually mean a slower, riskier site. DetailsEvery plugin adds code, requests and security risk. Most sites run faster and safer with fewer, well-chosen plugins.
MythWordPress is bad for SEO. FactWordPress is one of the best platforms for SEO. DetailsIt runs more websites than any other CMS and produces clean, crawlable HTML. Problems come from how a site is built, not from WordPress itself.
MythYou need a new theme to rank. FactMost sites can rank on the theme they have. DetailsSpeed, structure and content can usually be fixed on the current theme. A redesign is rarely the first fix, and it’s the most expensive one.
MythPage builders kill SEO. FactBuilders can rank when they’re set up well. DetailsElementor and Divi add weight, but with the right settings, caching and fewer add-ons, builder sites can pass Core Web Vitals.
MythA caching plugin solves speed. FactCaching is one part of speed, not all of it. DetailsHeavy images, scripts and slow hosting still hold pages back. Two caching plugins at once often make things worse.
MythTags help SEO. FactToo many tags usually hurt. DetailsHundreds of tag pages create thin near-duplicates of your posts. Most sites should limit tags or keep tag archives out of Google.
MythSEO is a one-time set-up. FactSEO keeps working only if you keep working on it. DetailsPlugin updates, new content and competitors keep changing the picture. Sites that keep improving keep ranking.

attrs.title: WordPress SEO questions, answered
attrs.lead: Can’t find your answer? Ask us on a free 30-minute call.

items.question: Is WordPress good for SEO?
items.answer: Yes. WordPress produces clean, crawlable HTML and has excellent SEO plugins. Most problems come from what’s been added over the years: too many plugins, heavy page builders, slow hosting and archive pages that nobody set up.

items.question: Do I still need an SEO plugin?
items.answer: Usually yes, but only one. Yoast SEO or Rank Math handles titles, sitemaps and basic schema well when it’s set up properly. Running two at once causes duplicate tags.

items.question: Yoast or Rank Math: which is better?
items.answer: Both work. We keep the one you have unless it’s causing problems, and set it up for your site rather than leaving the defaults on.

items.question: Will you change my theme or page builder?
items.answer: Only if it’s the cause of the problem. Most sites can be made fast on their current theme. If a builder is too heavy, we’ll show you the numbers and the options.

items.question: Do you work with WooCommerce?
items.answer: Yes. We fix product and category pages, variation URLs, filters and product schema. For larger stores, see our eCommerce SEO services.

items.question: How much do WordPress SEO services cost?
items.answer: A fix sprint and monthly SEO are both a fixed price, based on the size of your site and what it needs. We quote after a free 30-minute call.

items.question: How long until we see results?
items.answer: Speed and indexing fixes often show within weeks. Rankings and traffic from new and improved pages usually build over three to six months.

items.question: Do you need access to our WordPress admin?
items.answer: Not to start: our first review uses public data. For the work itself we need an editor or admin login, and ideally a staging site.
